kartice.povzetek_sl: The role of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) in the emergence of visual stimuli into conscious awareness remains contested. Additionally, whether top-down prefrontal connectivity is shaped by prior expectations during this process is not well understood. To address these questions, we applied dynamic causal modelling (DCM) to an EEG dataset during breaking continuous flash suppression (bCFS), which offers tight control over when a stimulus breaks into conscious perception. Our network comprised bilateral PFC, primary visual cortex, fusiform gyrus and motor cortex. Because perceptual breakthrough precedes behavioural report, we used a temporally resolved classifier to empirically define each participants moment of perceptual breakthrough (M = 1250ms, SD = 100ms). kartice.naslov: Paternal transmission of the APPPS1 transgene is associated with increased amyloid pathology and a small Thy1.2-APP methylation difference
kartice.povzetek_sl:
Maternal transmission of the APP transgene lowers amyloid burden in 5xFAD mice. We examined whether APPPS1-21 shows a similar parent-of-origin association and whether Thy1.2 methylation contributes. F1 offspring inheriting the transgene from the mother had less A{beta}42, fewer plaques, less gliosis, and less human APP at intermediate ages. The A{beta}42 difference was not detected in the F2 cohort at 100 days. Non-transgenic off-spring of APPPS1 mothers did not differ in glial counts, and serum anti-A{beta} antibody levels were not higher at 40 days. In an exploratory methylation analysis of 32 brains, parent-of-origin-associated differences were sex-specific and enriched on chromosome X, not chromosome 2. The Thy1.2-APP cassette showed an approximately three-percentage-point paternal increase; the PSEN1 cassette did not. These findings establish an association with parental transmission but do not show that methylation causes the pathology differences.

kartice.naslov: ProteoBridge Connects Proteomics Quantification Outputs to Reusable Analysis Workflows
kartice.povzetek_sl: Quantification tools for bottom-up label-free proteomics, including DIA-NN, Spectronaut, MaxQuant, and FragPipe, use different table layouts, column headers, modification notations, and parameter files. Downstream applications maintain separate readers for these outputs. ProteoBridge lets an application request the same quantity, such as unnormalized ion intensity, across reports from different quantification tools. JSON parsing rules describe each tools tables, and software-specific parameter parsers read the settings. The rules currently cover 14 tools and are tested on public inputs. A shared parser organizes the reported quantities into one level for each feature type the tool reports (fragments, ions, peptidoforms, peptides, or proteins) and writes the result as AnnData/MuData, Parquet, or DuckDB. A JSON summary records the structure, provenance, and conversion warnings, such as unmapped modifications. Applications can use the apb-catalog API in Python, R, or TypeScript to map the requested quantity to the field that holds it for each tool and version. kartice.naslov: Prethalamus integrates neocortical and hypothalamic input to promote courage
kartice.povzetek_sl: Courage, the ability to act despite potential danger, is essential for adaptive behavior, yet the circuit mechanisms that balance caution and risk-taking under threat are not fully understood. Here we identify the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus (vLGN), an inhibitory prethalamic structure, as a key node in this process. High vLGN activity predicts courageous behavior, such as leaving a shelter to enter a potentially threatening environment, and optogenetic activation of vLGN neurons promotes risk-taking under diverse aversive conditions. Inputs to vLGN from retrosplenial cortex (RSC) and ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) modulate this behavior in opposing directions: RSC input promotes leaving safety, while VMH input suppresses it. These inputs target largely distinct vLGN populations that interact to integrate these opposing drives: a hypothalamic signal promoting defensive caution and a neocortical signal promoting action despite potential threat.

kartice.povzetek_sl: Brain biomechanical connectivity (BC) captures shared regional viscoelastic properties that may support functional interactions. Although functional and structural brain networks are well characterized, the systems-level organization of brain biomechanics remains unknown. Using in-vivo magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) and community detection, we established BC and its network organization across the mouse lifespan, spanning seven stages from early adolescence (4 weeks) to old age (72 weeks). BC was benchmarked against established functional and structural connectivity, revealing shared connectivity features. Biomechanical network organization showed increasing segregation during adolescence, peaking in late adolescence, followed by progressive reintegration with aging. kartice.povzetek_sl: A ubiquitous property of physical and biological systems is scale-free dynamics in which spectral power decreases as a function of frequency, showing a 1/f spectral slope. The 1/f slope of neural power spectra has been proposed as a marker of cortical excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance, based on pharmacological experiments and computational models of synaptic activity in cortical networks. Here, we show that this slope can be volitionally modulated and that its modulation is accompanied by changes in motor cortical activity reflecting E/I balance. kartice.povzetek_sl: IntroductionAn ongoing neural circuit excitation (E) and inhibition (I) imbalance is thought to be a major contributor to clinical conditions such as autism, schizophrenia, and epilepsy. Current methods for directly measuring E:I dynamics require invasive procedures that are difficult to perform in non-human animals and nearly impossible in humans. A non-invasive measure of E:I balance is of great interest as a diagnostic as well as therapeutic marker, and as a means of studying relevant pathological and intervention mechanisms. Scientists have recently developed a computational model to show that, using resting-state (RS) MEG or EEG recordings, the E:I balance can be estimated from the power law exponent (slope) of the electrophysiological power spectrum. In their model, the RS power spectrum exponent is hypothesized to reflect the integration of synaptic currents in the brain, an index of E:I balance driven largely by excitatory (glutamate, Glu) and inhibitory (gamma-aminobutyric acid, GABA) neurotransmitter levels. kartice.naslov: From cellular synaptic input profiles to population-level respiratory circuitry
kartice.povzetek_sl:
Breathing depends on coordinated activity among brainstem neurons. Their discharge patterns show when populations are active but do not specify the synaptic inputs that generate these patterns. Assuming that respiratory pattern generation involves a small number of interacting populations distinguished by discharge timing and excitatory or inhibitory output, we used synaptic conductances as readouts of their convergent activity. We reconstructed excitatory and inhibitory conductances from our previously described in situ rat brainstem-spinal cord recording archive (168 recordings, 150 neurons). We represented candidate presynaptic activity by five independently recorded population discharge patterns, assuming that phase-dependent inputs originated within these populations. We fitted each conductance time course as a nonnegative weighted sum of these patterns and tested whether candidate inputs could be omitted from the population mean, using variation across cells.

Post-inspiratory inhibition was supported in all three inspiratory populations.
